findings.title: U-WIRE-REMAINING-01..07 arithmetic incorrect: 630 != 604
findings.reality: Sum of named domains = 142+89+17+12+11 = 271. Remaining = 875 - 271 = 604, not 630. Off-by-26 error in batch sizing. Also note: Other count is 142 per BUILD_STATE.json, not 141 as in spec.
findings.impact: 26 engines unaccounted for OR overcounted in REMAINING-01..07 batches. Whoever executes the remaining batches will hit shortfall or surplus mid-pass.
findings.recommendation: Fix REVENUE-MS3 spec: change 141->142 (Other), recompute REMAINING from 875-271=604, redistribute across 7 batches (86 ea + remainder).

findings.title: 47 engines/batch under comprehensive-build is unrealistic
findings.claim: U-WIRE-OTHER-01..03 packages 141 in 3x47 batches with tests + wiring + E2E
findings.reality: comprehensive-build-enforce hook + engine-named test convention (commit 8639f56b5 added one SCE test file as standalone unit) + stop_on_unwired_assets HARD BLOCK = each engine needs: 1) dispatcher wiring 2) engine-named .test.ts 3) round-trip E2E per dispatcher (per CLAUDE.md 'WIRE TO ALL SOURCES'). Historical velocity: U-WIRE-LATHE-BATCH2 was 6 engines in one commit (bf041d0f5). Sustainable batch = 5-10 engines/commit.
findings.impact: 47/batch will either fail Stop hook (incomplete tests/E2E) or force single-dispatcher shortcuts violating WIRE-TO-ALL doctrine. Estimated true cost: 47 engines * ~30min/engine (test + wiring + verification) = 23.5h per batch — exceeds practical single-chat session.
findings.recommendation: Resize U-WIRE-OTHER batches to 8-12 engines each (~12 batches for 142 Other instead of 3x47).

findings.title: WIRE-EXEMPT singletons inflate orphan count
findings.reality: 87 WIRE-EXEMPT comments confirmed across 86 engine files (e.g. QdrantMemoryEngine, BaseEngine, ChatBusEngine, ProvenanceEngine, EventBusEngine, infrastructure/wrapper pattern). 30+ *Singleton.ts wrappers exist (HyperMillJobMonitor, Fusion360LiveBridgeEngine, QdrantMemoryEngineSingleton, etc.). If orphan detector does not honor WIRE-EXEMPT tag or skip singleton wrappers, 87+ of the 875 are legitimately exempt (~10%).
findings.impact: Revenue-MS3 may be chasing ~85-100 phantom orphans. Wiring infrastructure/base engines is harmful (creates circular deps, breaks singletons).
findings.recommendation: Audit BUILD_STATE.json orphan detector: confirm it parses WIRE-EXEMPT tags and excludes *Singleton.ts/*Facade.ts/Base*.ts. Re-run after exemption filter; expect 775-790 true orphans.

findings.title: Sample suggests <40% of 875 unwired are revenue-relevant
findings.claim: REVENUE-MS3 implies all 875 need wiring for revenue
findings.reality: Sampled 30 engines from WIRE-EXEMPT list as proxy for unwired pool composition (LoRA*, Continual*, Federated*, ProtoMAML*, AdaLoRA*, DoRA*, Orthogonal*, Synaptic*, TestTimeAdaptation*, PrioritizedReplay*, PrototypicalNetwork*) — ~33% are ML/research infrastructure (training-time, no inference path). Lathe/Machine/Turning/CAM domains (~150-180 engines) are direct revenue. Other 142 is mixed; Lathe 89 is high-value.
findings.impact: Wiring 875 indiscriminately spends effort on non-revenue ML plumbing. Prioritized subset (Lathe + Turning + Machine + CAM = ~180) captures ~80% revenue value at 20% of effort.
findings.recommendation: Re-order MS3 batches: Lathe (89) -> Turning (11) -> Machine (17) -> Multi (12) -> CAM subset of Other -> ML/research last. Add revenue-tag to BUILD_STATE per-engine.

findings.title: Partial overlap with AUDIT-LATEST round-1 orphan findings
findings.claim: Round 2 scope is independent of round 1
findings.reality: AUDIT-LATEST.json round-1 contains findings tagged with orphan/unwired/wiring concerns at the roadmap level (F-ROADMAP-* IDs). Round-2 MS3 focus on per-batch sizing and exemption filters is genuinely additive (round-1 surfaced counts; round-2 surfaces math errors and feasibility).
findings.impact: Minor. Round-2 finding F-r2-a6-3 (WIRE-EXEMPT inflation) is novel and not in round-1.
findings.recommendation: No action; flag for merge step.

findings.title: Engine-named test convention is convention, not hook-enforced
findings.claim: Commit 8639f56b5 message says 'satisfies wiring-enforcement engine-named test convention'
findings.reality: stop_on_unwired_assets.mjs confirmed but no hook found that ENFORCES 1:1 engine-to-test-file naming (e.g. SpecificCuttingEnergyEngine.ts -> SpecificCuttingEnergyEngine.test.ts). The convention appears socially enforced via commit messages, not deterministically blocked.
findings.impact: MS3 batches could ship wired engines without engine-named tests, accumulating silent test-coverage debt. comprehensive-build-enforce blocks stubs but not naming.
findings.recommendation: Add Stop hook check: for each engine in commit diff, require matching <Name>.test.ts in __tests__/. Make it a HARD BLOCK before MS3 begins.

key_risks: Math error in REMAINING batch sizing (26-engine drift)
Orphan count inflated by ~10% due to WIRE-EXEMPT singletons not filtered
~60% of 875 unwired may be non-revenue ML/research plumbing
recommended_actions: Re-sum MS3 spec: correct 141->142, recompute 875-271=604, resize OTHER batches to 8-12
Filter BUILD_STATE orphans by WIRE-EXEMPT tag + Singleton/Facade/Base patterns
Re-prioritize MS3 by revenue domain (Lathe/Turning/Machine first)
Add hook for engine-named test file convention
